propositions: Writes are relation-scoped (add_dependency keyed on target_id+relation), but removal is pair-scoped (_get_link_info returns only most recent net-active link), causing asymmetry when one pair holds two differently-related net-active links (e.g. blocks+relates_to)

Inbound removal of one relation in a double-related pair reaches G5 guard and declines permanently because pair-scoped unlink finds the other relation as most-recent, causing re-emission and re-decline on every reconcile pass with no convergence

Guard G4 (same-pass link suppression) fails to suppress the inbound remove when outbound dedupes direction-agnostically on vendor_type, leaving no link mutation for the pair and allowing the removal record to survive to G5

Removal must become relation-scoped (keyed on target_id+relation) symmetric with the write path, with optional relation argument to CLI and library (no-relation defaults to pair-scoped for backward compatibility)

Safety invariant: relation-scoped removal removes only links with exactly matching (target_id, relation); a removal naming a relation with no net-active local link is a logged no-op and removes nothing
A double-related pair converges when one relation is removed via relation-scoped seam, with the mirrored relation's link gone, the other relation surviving, and re-apply idempotent
